title: R10 — What the language refuses to say

props.covers: The operation language carries concrete geometry rather than abstract align, fan, grid, or gap constraints; the aesthetic supplies relational intent, while fresh digests and renders provide the evidence used to judge it.

text.insert: R10 — What the language refuses to say

The operation surface expresses concrete entities, and every geometry edit uses a complete finite rectangle. It has no align, fan, lattice, equal-gap, or importance-size field; those meanings come from deliberate repeated geometry, section structure, labels, and color.

defines the relational vocabulary: same size plus same gap means peers, a larger box means more important, an off-register box means exception, and a parent centers over its children. The agent realizes those relations with explicit geometry, copying exact peer size and pitch from the latest BOARD digest. Patched rectangles snap to the 16px grid as quantization. Every successful

result is sized to its own operation; a look returns the whole board, and a refused call carries only its error lines, so a look is how the board is recovered. No diagnostic enforces abstract peer alignment or equal-gap intent: the always-on diagnostics guard physical readability, and the renders remain the composition judge.
